introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. English Language 2 (0730), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Paper 2: Section A - Summary and Text Reconstruction; Section B - Composition; Section C - Prescribed Texts. Duration: three hours.**

Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet, beginning each section on a new page.

Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks.

Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty.

In the SUMMARY question, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will be penalised.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

A pre-prepared or memorised composition will be severely sanctioned.

incertitudes: Regle de choix : la page de garde impose « Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet ». La Section A est obligatoire (aucune regle) ; `regles_choix` porte une regle `parmi 1 sur 6` pour la Section B (sujets a a f) et `parmi 1 sur 4` pour la Section C (questions 1 a 4), identiques dans les 12 fichiers.

Aucun corrige officiel : les corriges sont des reponses modeles redigees pour ce lot. Les resumes et compositions sont comptes par script ; la section C (Prescribed texts) est traitee uniquement avec ce que le sujet imprime (voir les fichiers C1 a C4).
Points : section A 30 (resume 15 + reconstruction 15), section B 20, section C 20, imprimes dans le sujet. Aucun ecart constate.

Resume : le passage est recopie en entier (9 paragraphes) avec l'orthographe imprimee, y compris « utilize » et « utilising », « contents » (pluriel imprime), « fact-finding » et la faute imprimee « Such a phenomena leverages » (recopiee telle quelle). Le sujet imprime « social media » avec « the » (« on the social media »), recopie tel quel. Le resume modele compte 142 mots (limite : 150 mots en deux paragraphes au plus).
Le bareme interne des 15 points du resume n'est pas imprime dans le sujet : la grille du corrige est indicative.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**QUESTION 1: SUMMARY (15 marks)**

*Read the following text on the social media and using your own words as far as possible, summarize it in not more than two paragraphs of 150 words.*

Social media is a computer-based technology that facilitates sharing of ideas, thoughts and information through the building of virtual networks and communities. By design, social media is internet-based and gives users quick electronic communication of content. Content includes personal information, documents, videos and photos. Users engage with social media via computer, tablet or smartphone via a web-based software or web application, often utilising it for messaging.

Social media originated as a way to interact with friends and family but was later adopted by business which wanted to take advantage of a popular new communication method to reach out to customers. The power of social media is the ability to connect and share information with anyone on earth, or with many people simultaneously.

Globally, there are more than 3 billion social media users. Social media is an ever-changing and ever-evolving web-based platform. According to Pew Research Centre, social media users tend to be younger. Nearly 90% of people between the ages of 18 and 29 use at least one form of social media. Further, these users tend to be better educated and relatively wealthy.

Social media may take the form of a variety of tech-enabled activities. These activities include photo sharing, blogging, social gaming, social networks, video sharing, business networks, virtual worlds, reviews and much more. Even governments and politicians utilize social media to engage constituents and voters.

For individuals, social media is used to keep in touch with friends and extended family. Some people will use various social media applications to network career opportunities, find people across the globe with like interests, and share their thoughts, feelings, insight and emotions. Those who engage in these activities are part of a virtual network.

For businesses, social media is an indispensable tool. Companies use the platform to find and engage with customers, drive sales through advertising and promotion, gauge customer trends, and offer customer service and support.

Social media's role in helping businesses is significant. It facilitates communication with customers, enabling the melding of social interactions on e-commerce sites. Its ability to collect information helps focus on marketing efforts and market research. It helps in promoting products and services, as it enables the distribution of targeted, timely and exclusive sales and coupons to would-be customers. Further, social media can help in building customer relationships through loyalty programmes linked to social media.

While social media has its negative side, many point to the platform and call out negative features, likening its overuse to an addiction. Some contest it contributes to inattentiveness, stress, and jealousy. The National Centre for Biotechnology Information links heavy social media use to depression. Also, many times, social media may be a conduit for misleading information and falsehood.

The 2016 American Presidential Election has well-documented accounts of the impact of the ability to spread information through the platform. Such a phenomena leverages the power of social media, allowing anyone to reach an audience of millions with contents that lack oversight or fact-finding.

*(www. Investopedia .com. Maya E Dollarhide [updated September 6, 2020])*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model summary (two paragraphs, 142 words)**

Social media is internet-based technology, used on computers, tablets and phones, that lets people share ideas, information and content through virtual networks. It began as a way for friends and families to interact, but businesses soon adopted it, and its power lies in linking anyone on earth, or many people at once. Over three billion people use it, mostly young, educated and fairly wealthy, and it takes many forms, such as blogging, gaming and video sharing, which even governments and politicians exploit.

Individuals use it to keep in touch, look for careers, find people with similar interests and express their feelings. For businesses it is indispensable: they reach customers, advertise, study markets, offer targeted promotions, build loyalty and give support. However, critics link heavy use to addiction, stress, jealousy and depression, and it can spread falsehood, as the 2016 American election showed.

**Content points expected** (the passage contains about a dozen; a good summary keeps the main ones, each in the candidate's own words)

1. Social media is internet-based technology that lets people share ideas, information and content (personal information, documents, videos, photos) through virtual networks, using a computer, tablet or smartphone.
2. It began as a way for friends and family to interact, then businesses adopted it to reach customers; its power is to connect anyone on earth, or many people at once.
3. It has more than 3 billion users, who tend to be young (nearly 90% of 18 to 29 year olds), better educated and relatively wealthy.
4. It takes many forms (photo sharing, blogging, gaming, networks, video sharing and others) and is used even by governments and politicians.
5. Individuals use it to keep in touch, to network for careers, to find people with like interests and to share feelings.
6. For businesses it is indispensable: finding and engaging customers, advertising and promotion, gauging trends, customer service, market research, targeted offers, loyalty programmes.
7. It has a negative side: overuse likened to addiction, inattentiveness, stress, jealousy, depression, and the spread of misleading information (the 2016 American Presidential Election).

**Marking grid (15 marks).** The paper prints only the total. A summary is rewarded for (a) selecting the main points and leaving out detail and examples, (b) using its own words, (c) accurate, fluent and well-organised writing in no more than two paragraphs, and (d) respecting the limit of 150 words. The exact split of the 15 marks is not printed.

**Common mistakes**

1. Lifting whole sentences from the passage (the instructions say indiscriminate copying will be penalised); replace the passage's words by synonyms and rebuild the sentences.
2. Going over 150 words, or writing more than two paragraphs; count the words and cut the least important details (examples, figures, the source).
3. Adding comments or opinions instead of reporting the writer's ideas, or leaving out one whole side of the passage (here, the negative side of social media).
